Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash.text:
KILL_CLAIM: Opcode-sequence features—and any cheap chronology-derived journal feature—cannot recover the global contract co-reference topology: the organ-partition defined by which cells share BIND/LINK/VIEW/EFFECT slots as {route,quf,time} versus {crdt,proof,world}, because schedule-invariant per-cell journals expose only local op order, not many-to-many address incidence.
INSTRUMENT: CO-REF C1 ADDRESS-SWAP LEDGER: a deterministic fixture that holds op-token journals, schedules, payload multisets, and cell identities fixed while remapping contract slot addresses to permute the true organ graph, then scores bigram/trigram/Levenshtein/NW/SW, embeddings, and address-incidence features against the 3/3 partition oracle.
FALSIFIER: A chronology-only feature over the masked op journal (no cell IDs and no contract-address labels) predicts the true organ partition above chance across all four schedules/reseeded payloads, or predicts the address-permuted ground-truth partition from the unchanged op-only journal, proving the relation is in the sequence rather than only in addressing.
ARTIFACT_RISK: If descriptifying cell-specific call/state aliases collapses S1 to chance while preserving identity TF, or if the apparent address/incidence signal is reducible to cell-ID histograms, then the order-sensitivity and dialect-null receipts are lexical/identity artifacts, not evidence that the relation lives only in contract/runtime addressing.

inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash.text:
KILL_CLAIM: The **inter-cell role-adjacency topology** — the concrete relational structure is the partition of the 21 pairwise cell-pair relations among {route, crdt, time, quf, world, proof, engine} into cross-organ edges (between {route, quf, time} and {crdt, proof, world}) versus in-cell edges (within each organ). This is a graph structure that exists only in cross-cell relational space: no per-cell opcode-sequence feature (bigram/trigram TF, edit distance, alignment score, or any journal-derived statistic) can encode it, because each cell's journal is generated by an independent schedule with no cross-cell calls — the pairwise wiring is invisible to any single-node feature vector. Cheap features provably see only per-cell temporal order (P2 receipts: cross-cell schedule recovery p≤0.002) and provably cannot see which pairs of cells share an organ boundary, because that information is not in any individual journal but in the relation between journals — and cells never directly compare journals.

INSTRUMENT: A **role-shuffled journal reconstruction** — take the 7 cell journals, computationally invert the dialect partition (assign between-organs-style schedule statistics to in-cell cells and vice versa) while holding each cell's opcode multiset, schedule length, token distribution, and per-phase state trajectory fixed, then re-run all 5 instruments × 2 encodings × 4 schedules with the dialect bar. If cheap features were truly blind to role (as we claim), they should still fail on the inverted partition. If they suddenly succeed (recovering the new partition above chance), our original receipts were artifacts: the features were detecting a low-level correlate that happened to align with the true partition by coincidence. The instrument forces a prediction: genuine blindness means failure on inversion; artifact means success.

FALSIFIER: If any of the 5 instruments × 2 encodings × 4 schedules recovers the role-adjacency partition (cross-organ vs in-cell) above chance on the role-shuffled journals — specifically, if the dialect bar is passed (≥19/20 partitions correctly ranked) on even one instrument-encoding-schedule triple with p<0.05 — then my kill-claim is dead: cheap journal-derived features CAN capture role-adjacency topology, and the Wave-69 null result was a methodological failure rather than a genuine relational blind spot. Additionally: if cross-cell pair features (e.g., cosine similarity between route's and crdt's normalized opcode-journal vectors) show significant role-partition correlation (r>0.5, p<0.01, n=21 pairs), the topology is captured via interaction terms and the kill-claim collapses.

ARTIFACT_RISK: Schedule-length coupling. If the 4 schedules (A linear, B reverse, C interleave, D split-swap) produce different effective token-sequence lengths per cell — particularly schedule D (split-swap) which may interleave active and idle phases differently, creating cells with systematically different effective lengths depending on their organ — and if the dialect partition (between-organs vs in-cell) correlates with average per-cell sequence length, then the "dialect blindness" could be a length confound: cheap features might detect length variation that spuriously correlates with role, but the dialect bar tests partition recovery, not length prediction, so a length confound could mask genuine dialect signal by flooding the feature space with a non-dialect axis. The control: pad or truncate all schedules to identical token counts (using NOP-fill matched to the longest schedule across all 4 schedules × 7 cells = 28 sequences), re-run the P2 dialect bar test. If dialect recovery rises above chance on any instrument (≥19/20 partitions), the original blindness was a schedule-length artifact, not a genuine relational blind spot.

meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B.text:
KILL_CLAIM: the schedule-invariant contract-mediated relational topology / dialect role membership, specifically the between-organs {route,quf,time} vs in-cell {crdt,proof,world} 3/3 partition and the inter-cell dependency role it encodes, which is invariant under the four schedule permutations
INSTRUMENT: Contract-Slot Co-activation Graph with Dialect Role Probe CSCG-DRP, built from runtime addressing logs of shared contract touches per cell-pair and evaluated against op-token journal features under schedule-permuted A/B/C/D pairs with ground-truth dialect labels
FALSIFIER: bigram/trigram-TF cosine, Levenshtein, Needleman-Wunsch or Smith-Waterman over the raw per-cell op-token journal recovers the true 3/3 dialect partition at rank 1/20 with p<0.001 across all 5 instruments x 2 encodings x 4 schedules, or recovers cross-cell contract co-activation above chance under schedule permutation
ARTIFACT_RISK: schedule-length / duplicate-token coupling inflates order sensitivity: split-swap/interleave change journal length and repeat counts per cell so n-gram TF cos and edit distances track length/duplicates not order; control with length-normalized, duplicate-stripped journals and a length-matched random-permutation null preserving the payload multiset

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning.text:
KILL_CLAIM: The true relational structure of cell interactions—specifically the *topological graph* of directed edges between distinct cell IDs, including directionality, fan-in, and fan-out patterns across the 7-cell corpus.

INSTRUMENT: A "Topology Stress Test" using a contract payload consisting of a single directed chain of 7 hops (cell_1→cell_2→...→cell_7) versus a single star topology (cell_0→cell_1,2,3,4,5,6). If opcode-sequence features can distinguish these two fundamentally different interaction graphs from the same multiset of opcodes, they capture topology; if not, they are blind.

FALSIFIER: The observation that the feature vectors for the chain and star topologies are separable (e.g., L1 distance > threshold, or classifier accuracy > 95%) despite both having identical opcode multisets and schedule invariants. This would prove the features are sensitive to the relational graph, refuting the claim of blindness.

ARTIFACT_RISK: A length confound where the chain topology has 7 hops while the star has 6 hops total. The features might simply be counting opcodes or path length rather than modeling topology. The control is a "Topology Equivalence" test: generate a star with 7 hops (cell_0→cell_1→cell_2→cell_3→cell_4→cell_5→cell_6, plus a dummy leaf attached to cell_0) versus the 7-hop chain. If features distinguish these two topologies despite identical hop counts, the risk is exposed; if not, the features are truly length-insensitive and topology-blind.
